candidates.title: Voltage creeps up
candidates.story: An electrical part that is degrading (e.g. a winding or contactor) disturbs supply regulation, so the measured voltage drifts above its usual band before it gives out.
candidates.first_draft_rule: volt hourly reading > P99 of normal operation (all machines) for 3+ consecutive hours

candidates.title: Rotation sags
candidates.story: Wear or a seizing part adds friction and drag, so the shaft turns slower than usual for the same drive in the days before a mechanical failure.
candidates.first_draft_rule: rotate hourly reading < P1 of normal operation (all machines) for 3+ consecutive hours

candidates.title: Pressure builds
candidates.story: A sticking valve, clogged passage or failing seal restricts flow, so upstream pressure rises before the component fails.
candidates.first_draft_rule: pressure hourly reading > P99 of normal operation (all machines) for 3+ consecutive hours

candidates.title: Vibration rises
candidates.story: Bearing wear, misalignment or a loosening mount raises vibration amplitude well before a mechanical breakage.
candidates.first_draft_rule: vibration hourly reading > P99 of normal operation (all machines) for 3+ consecutive hours

candidates.title: Any signal drifts
candidates.story: Each component has its own physical signature (C01-C04). A machine-level alarm that watches all four at once should catch failures of any component.
candidates.first_draft_rule: any of [volt ↑, rotate ↓, pressure ↑, vibration ↑]: 24h trailing mean beyond P99 (↑) / P1 (↓) of normal operation (its own machine), in the arrow's direction

candidates.title: Any error code
candidates.story: Controllers log faults (overcurrent, stall, sensor out of range) when a part starts to misbehave; a recent error is an early, software-side symptom.
candidates.first_draft_rule: error-log count in last 24h > P95 of normal operation (all machines)

candidates.title: Overdue maintenance
candidates.story: Parts wear out with use; the longer since a part was last replaced, the closer it is to failing. This is a COUNTER (it only climbs, then resets at maintenance).
candidates.first_draft_rule: hours since maint. of the oldest component hourly reading > P99 of normal operation (all machines)

candidates.title: Drift confirmed by an error
candidates.story: An error code on its own is noisy and a signal drift on its own may be a sensor blip; requiring both within two days should keep the alarms that matter.
candidates.first_draft_rule: (any of [volt ↑, rotate ↓, pressure ↑, vibration ↑]: 24h trailing mean beyond P99 (↑) / P1 (↓) of normal operation (its own machine), in the arrow's direction) AND (error-log count in last 48h > P80 of normal operation (all machines))

candidates.title: Matched signature (part's own signal + own error)
candidates.story: A failing part shows up twice: its own physical signal drifts AND the controller logs the fault code tied to that part. A drift with an unrelated error code is probably a look-alike. The pairing is learned on dev machines only.
candidates.first_draft_rule: ((volt 24h trailing mean > P99 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (error1 count in last 48h > P80 of normal operation (all machines))) OR ((rotate 24h trailing mean < P1 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (error2+error3 count in last 48h > P80 of normal operation (all machines))) OR ((pressure 24h trailing mean > P99 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (error4 count in last 48h > P80 of normal operation (all machines))) OR ((vibration 24h trailing mean > P99 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (error5 count in last 48h > P80 of normal operation (all machines)))

candidates.title: Drift on an aging part
candidates.story: A part that has run long since its last replacement is worn; if its own signal starts to drift, that drift is more likely the start of a failure than a harmless excursion. Unlike C09 it does not wait for the error code, so it could warn earlier.
candidates.first_draft_rule: ((volt 24h trailing mean > P99 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (hours since maint. of comp1 hourly reading > P75 of normal operation (all machines))) OR ((rotate 24h trailing mean < P1 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (hours since maint. of comp2 hourly reading > P75 of normal operation (all machines))) OR ((pressure 24h trailing mean > P99 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (hours since maint. of comp3 hourly reading > P75 of normal operation (all machines))) OR ((vibration 24h trailing mean > P99 of normal operation (its own machine)) AND (hours since maint. of comp4 hourly reading > P75 of normal operation (all machines)))
